notes: Definitions: EBIT is modeled as Valero consolidated 'Operating income'; D&A is 'Depreciation and amortization expense'; capex is 'Capital expenditures (excluding VIEs)' (not total capital investments). ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/587626645/files/doc_financials/2024/q4/VLO-10K-Q4-2024.pdf))

NWC construction (used to populate historical NWC and forecast NWC % of sales): NWC = (Current assets - Cash and cash equivalents included in current assets) - Current liabilities, using the earnings-release balance sheet data for 2023-2025. ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))

Tax rate is the average effective tax rate computed from Income tax expense / income before income tax for 2023-2025 (model input, not explicitly disclosed as a single long-run rate). ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/587626645/files/doc_financials/2024/q4/VLO-10K-Q4-2024.pdf))

Comps limitation: EV/EBITDA values from the selected source are based on EV/TTM EBITDA (used as a proxy for EV/NTM EBITDA); EV/NTM Revenue was not available in the same dataset run, so it is set to null. ([valueinvesting.io](https://valueinvesting.io/MPC/valuation/ev_ebitda-multiples))
WACC, terminal growth, and terminal exit multiple are modeled assumptions for the DCF pipeline (not taken directly from management guidance).
NOLs: nol_balance was not retrieved in this run; left null and nol_utilization_pct is set to 0.80 as a placeholder per the schema template.

catalysts: Improvement in refining margins/product cracks and higher utilization/throughput volumes versus the near-term environment.
Capital project execution and turnaround timing that affects available capacity and margin capture.
Renewables and ethanol profitability shifts (including regulatory/credit dynamics) that can move segment-level EBIT closer to/away from the base case.
company_overview: Valero is a leading independent refiner producing transportation fuels and related products in the U.S., alongside renewable and low-carbon fuel activities. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/587626645/files/doc_financials/2024/q4/VLO-10K-Q4-2024.pdf))
Renewable Diesel and Ethanol segments expand Valero’s exposure beyond traditional refining cycles. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/587626645/files/doc_financials/2024/q4/VLO-10K-Q4-2024.pdf))

Valero operates with meaningful leverage to product crack spreads and throughput utilization, while funding sustaining capital and shareholder returns through operating cash flow. ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))
current_context: In 2025, Valero reported total revenues of 122.687B and operating income (EBIT proxy) of 3.181B. ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))

2025 operating cash flow was 5.826B, while capital expenditures (excluding VIEs) were 0.719B; Valero also reported 4.0B of stockholder cash returns for 2025. ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))

Valero ended 2025 with 4.7B cash and 8.3B total debt (excluding VIEs). ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes gradual convergence of EBIT margins upward from 2025’s trough toward a mid-cycle target (0.038 by 2030), consistent with downstream cyclical normalization rather than a linear forecast. ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))

Sustaining capex is modeled at ~0.55%–0.58% of sales, anchored to historical capital expenditures excluding VIEs. ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))

Working-capital intensity is normalized downward from the 2025 spike by using a NWC % of sales profile closer to 2023–2024 levels. ([investorvalero.com](https://investorvalero.com/news/news-details/2026/Valero-Energy-Reports-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-Results/default.aspx))

Valuation cross-check uses downstream peer EV/EBITDA ranges as a sanity check on terminal economics (acknowledging that comps use EV/TTM EBITDA as a proxy for NTM). ([valueinvesting.io](https://valueinvesting.io/MPC/valuation/ev_ebitda-multiples))
key_risks: Downside volatility in refining margins (crack spreads), feedstock differentials, and product demand.
Execution/regulatory risks (including environmental and low-carbon fuel policy changes) that could pressure returns on capital.
Working-capital swings (inventories and other current balances) that differ from the modeled NWC % of sales normalization.
